_about: What askdnd fills into Workshop's reviews (app/fft/reviews.json; Roadmap item 46, the pass's first change: a review is Workshop's, each product fills in its own). against: what Dig into a feature can check a feature against; devices: where a run looks; depths: how far it goes, with about how long. The characters come from the campaign's own (app/fft/host.py `review_characters`). how: askdnd's playbook for each review, the steps Claude follows when it runs one (`feedback.py review next` prints them).

against.label: How it's meant to work (its section of the map)

game_night: Play Battle, Sheet, Party and Table rolls on the local copy of beta as each player and the DM would on a game night (scripts/pull_beta.sh first if it's over a day old): a fight, a rest, a spell, an item, a level's worth of buttons.
A laptop first (1280×800), then a phone (375) for the pages players use at the table.
Each thing that slowed a player, confused them or broke: an issue under its feature (feedback.py note, then sort), with a picture.
Fix only what's small and Ship-lane in the run, through the usual pull request and check.
polish_area: Read the area's every page against docs/DESIGN.md and the design system page, and its section of docs/MAP.md for what it's for.
Open each page as everyone who uses it (admin, DM, player, View as), at a laptop width and the devices asked; keyboard only once; text at 200%.
Draw what should change as a mockup with picks (the picks block), asked in For you about the area; rounds until it's one piece.
Each change agreed becomes that area's batch: one design, one pull request, its checks.
every_number: For each of the four characters and the test sheets: every number and button on Battle against the 2024 books' own words (private/books) and the character's D&D Beyond sheet.
scripts/battle_audit.py and scripts/roll_coverage.py first; then by hand what they can't see.
A number that's wrong: an issue under its feature, with the book's page and the sheet's value; never the book's text in the repo.
Report what was covered, character by character.
dig_feature: Start from what was asked: the feature's open issues, then the words given.
Read the feature's section of docs/MAP.md and its code; check it against what was asked (the books, the sheet, the house rules, the map), with the characters asked, on the device asked.
Ask in For you (feedback.py ask review <run>, then review <run> wait <question>) only a real choice: which reading the table follows.
Each finding an issue under the feature; a small Ship-lane fix may go in the run; the rest in its area's batch.
the_week: Skip it (review <run> skip) when no pull request merged since the last run (feedback.py pulls --all).
Read the week's merged pull requests as one: fresh reviewers on the design system and the code (the code review on the week's combined diff).
Sweep every page (scripts/visual_compare.py against last week's main, scripts/layout_sweep.py).
Check Help's About and FAQ, the DM guide and the tour against what changed; each mismatch an issue.
rethink_build: Knowing every requirement now, read the architecture (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/MAP.md, the biggest modules) and ask: would we build it the same way?
Write what to keep, change and plan, each with its cost and what it buys.
Draw it as a page with picks for Brett (a decision, asked in For you); nothing changes until he picks.
test_tests: Mutation testing on the core modules changed since the last run (scripts/mutation.py), and every survivor that isn't wording gets a test.
The tests that passed only on a second try (GitHub's run summaries), and the slowest ones: each fixed at its cause.
Untested corners: branch coverage under 90% by file; an issue for each that matters.
who_sees: Read as an attacker and an auditor would: every route's refusals and readings (tests/test_refusals.py, tests/test_reading.py), what a request can change, what leaves askdnd (Claude, S3, email, Sentry).
What's kept, where and for how long: transcripts let go, backups restorable (the restore drill), keys still narrow (Railway, GitHub, the extension).
Each finding an issue under its feature; anything serious tells Brett at once.
runs_well: Sentry's errors of the month, the slowest pages (scripts/page_speed.py), failed jobs (Backstage › Sync, Development › Scheduled), and the month's costs (Claude, OpenAI, Railway and its worker).
One look: what's getting worse, and what to change.
Each finding an issue under its feature; a cost that's grown asked in For you.
how_we_work: Where time went this month (session lengths, what waited on whom: Development › Handoffs), what fell through (gaps, missed handoffs), what to change in Workshop.
The Roadmap: items gone stale, scopes waiting, whether the order still matches what matters.
Reviews that found nothing three runs in a row: suggest running them less often.
Drawn as a page with picks for Brett, asked in For you.
